newsitem.title: USA: Clinton says U.S. to take part in new Bosnia force.
newsitem.headline: Clinton says U.S. to take part in new Bosnia force.

text.p: President Bill Clinton said on Friday the United States has agreed in principle to take part in a follow-up international military force to help cement peace in Bosnia next year.

"I have decided to instruct the United States representative to NATO to inform our allies that in principle the United States will take part in a follow-on force in Bosnia," Clinton told a news conference at the White House.

He said Washington would contribute about 8,500 troops to the new NATO-led force. That total would be reviewed every six months and be cut to about half by the end of 1997. The force would withdraw completely by about June, 1998, he said.

Clinton had earlier said the U.S. troops would be out by the end of this year. But he said although the military mission in the war-ravaged country had been succesful, the reconstruction of the administration and the economy had been slower than expected, making a follow-on force necessary.

NATO sources said the new international force is expected to total 25,000 to 30,000 troops. Most of the 16 NATO nations had already informally approved the new force to replace the current NATO-led peace implementation force (IFOR) of 50,000 troops, now being withdrawan from Bosnia under a December 20 deadline.
